Intrinsic validation of a built table

Source: R/md-validate.R
md_validate.Rd

The gate for every ingest phase. These are properties the database is checked against on its own terms - key uniqueness, EIN wellformedness, referential integrity, provenance completeness, and agreement between the stored derived columns and a live npnormalize::np_normalize() call.

Usage

md_validate(
  x,
  key = NULL,
  ein = "ein",
  parent = NULL,
  enums = list(),
  required = character(),
  sample = 1000L
)

md_validate_report(v, stop_on_fail = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A data.frame/data.table to check.

key

Column(s) forming the primary key. Checked for uniqueness and completeness.

ein

Name of the EIN column, or NULL to skip the EIN checks.

parent

Optional vector of valid EINs (typically entity$ein) for a referential-integrity check.

enums

Named list of allowed values, e.g. list(variant_class = c("legal", "dba")).

required

Columns that must be present and wholly non-missing. Provenance columns belong here.

sample

Rows to draw for the derived-column agreement check. 0 skips it.

v

Output of md_validate().

stop_on_fail

Error rather than return when any check fails. Phase gates use TRUE; interactive inspection uses FALSE.

Value

A data.frame with one row per check: check, pass, n_bad, detail.

Details

It is deliberately not a comparison against a previously built artifact. matchdb is built from the freshest available sources, so "matches the file we had before" is not a property worth having: it would pin the database to an older vintage and to a build nobody can reproduce. Attribution against the existing pfmatch reference belongs at cutover, where it is a question about two references rather than a constraint on this one.
